title: RS_Union
description: >
  Returns one raster holding the bands of two to seven rasters, in argument
  order.
kernels:
  - returns: raster
    args: [raster, raster]
  - returns: raster
    args: [raster, raster, raster]
  - returns: raster
    args: [raster, raster, raster, raster]
  - returns: raster
    args: [raster, raster, raster, raster, raster]
  - returns: raster
    args: [raster, raster, raster, raster, raster, raster]
  - returns: raster
    args: [raster, raster, raster, raster, raster, raster, raster]
---

## Description

The result holds every band of the first raster, then every band of the second,
and so on. Each band keeps its own pixel type, nodata value and name, so rasters
of different pixel types can be joined. The rasters must have the same width
and height; the result takes the first raster's georeference and CRS, and the
others' are not checked. A NULL raster gives a NULL result.

No pixel is read: bands are carried over as they are, so joining rasters that
are still out-of-database does not load them.

## Examples

```sql
SELECT RS_NumBands(RS_Union(RS_Example(), RS_Example()));
```
